records.summary: China Turns To Iraqi Oil As US Blockade Chokes Iranian Supply Authored by Irina Slav via OilPrice.com , Chinese independent refiners are seeking crude oil cargoes from Iraq using the services of global commodity trading houses in a departure from their usual oil-sourcing practices, Bloomberg has reported, noting the continued U.S. blockade on Iranian ports. The so-called teapots have for years enjoyed discounted Iranian and Russian crude, but this year, the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran upended supply chains; the U.S. blockade paralyzed Iranian oil exports and Russian crude became more expensive . So, the teapots are buying crude from Iraq via commodity trading majors. "Iraqi crude has emerged as a winner during this period," Liao Na, founder of energy research firm GL Consulting, told Bloomberg. "This could entice other Persian Gulf suppliers to follow suit. After all, teapots remain one of the few pockets of resilient demand in an oversupplied market." records.summary: Bibi Loses The Gavel As Arab Votes Hand Eisenkot Control Of The Knesset Benjamin Netanyahu's camp lost its hold on Israel's parliament on Tuesday night, when the Knesset voted 66-52 to make Yashar's Matan Kahana speaker, ousting Likud's Amir Ohana after a filibuster of more than six hours by the outgoing coalition failed to stop the vote . Kahana won on the votes of the Arab-majority parties. Without Ra'am and the Joint List, which hold 19 seats, the four parties of Gadi Eisenkot's bloc had 48 votes, four fewer than the 52 that went to Likud's candidate, coalition whip Ofir Katz. Only Ra'am's Yasser Hujeirat missed the vote on Kahana's side; Katz took 52 of the Netanyahu bloc's 53 votes, with Likud's Nir Barkat absent. Eisenkot called the result a "proper democratic move which reflects the absolute majority who voted for change." Likud called it "a low point in the history of the Knesset" and said Kahana had been elected with the votes of "terror supporters." Members of Netanyahu's bloc shouted "shame" at each Arab lawmaker who voted for Kahana, according to CNN . Mountain View-based robotaxi provider Waymo is testing its new Zeekr M-Vision vehicles in San Francisco before adding them to its existing fleet.Craig Lee/The Examiner  The order is dated Nov. 11, but it surfaced only on Tuesday, when the San Francisco Business Times reported it. It restricts both Waymo's deployment and driverless testing permits, barring the company from running any car without a human driver on a California freeway, and it has no end date: the DMV says it stays in place "until Waymo demonstrates to the Department that it has taken effective corrective actions." records.title: Touch of evil: the terrifying truth about sleep paralysis
records.summary: One in five people have experienced this frightening state – and the Harvard neuroscientist Baland Jalal has dedicated his career to studying it. Could it be a portal to a deeper understanding of the mind? The Harvard neuroscientist Baland Jalal is considering the unfathomable depths of the human brain. “It can contemplate itself, and vast galaxies, spirits, souls, poetry, Einstein. Yet you hold it in your hand and it seems so trivial.” Jalal’s passion – the subject that drove him to become a scientist – is sleep paralysis, a brain glitch that can fill its host with terror so palpable that it can cause lasting trauma. “What you get very close to in sleep paralysis,” he says, “is that subjective world of the mind. It’s very hard to put into words.” He should know – he’s spent 271 pages trying to do so. His new book, The Phantom Mind, argues that by exploring the borderlands of sleep, where sleep paralysis occurs, we can delve deeper into how all aspects of our minds work. He may wear a lab coat and examine brain regions and neurochemicals, but studying the mechanics, he says, doesn’t damp down the mysteries of consciousness. “For me, actually, I’ve become more spiritual and interested in the world of mystery and, I want to say supernatural, but dimensions that are intangible, by studying something like sleep paralysis.” Continue reading...

Boulos, a London-based Lebanese journalist working for the BBC , and Habak, a Syrian activist and cameraman, first connected while covering the Syrian civil war and stayed in touch through years of war, revolution and exile, forming a relationship that is chronicled in the documentary by drawing on 13 years of their personal videos, voice notes and other correspondence. The film also examines the unequal relationship between international news organizations and local journalists whose work they rely on, the fraught political history between Syria and Lebanon, and how Boulos and Habak’s personal connection overcame those divisions. “Without our journalistic relationship, [we] would have never been together. I would have never opened my heart to somebody like him,” says Boulos. “We can be any race, any gender, any religion, any background, but at the same time we’re all humans.” Birds of War premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Documentary Special Jury Award for Journalistic Impact.

His most impactful relationship, however, would prove to be with a young Donald Trump, whom he mentored in business and politics during the 1970s and ’80s. records.title: 9/11 vets: Do politicians take the decision to go to war seriously?
records.summary: It is Veterans Day again, which means that, alongside the free red, white, and blue pancake specials and complimentary coffees, Americans will post tributes honoring the ultimate sacrifice of our soldiers. Just as predictably, on Memorial Day, veterans will receive well-intentioned messages thanking them for their service. Of course, Memorial Day honors those who died while serving in the U.S. military, whereas Veterans Day recognizes all who have served. This confusion is hardly something to get worked up about in itself. But it is symptomatic of something more consequential: a nation detached from its military and the wars it fights. In a sense, Americans are not wrong to conflate the two holidays. Service and sacrifice cannot be neatly separated, especially when the military has become an instrument of statecraft, diplomacy, humanitarian assistance, and lethal force whose deployment increasingly depends less on congressional authorization than on the decisions of a single president. methodology.reliability: A official primary source/catalogue; B established newsroom or independent research; C specialist, advocacy or aggregator; D alternative commentary; E unverified social/community; U unclassified. Grade describes source class, not the truth of a specific claim.
methodology.confidence: Claim confidence is left unassessed unless an upstream collector supplies a numeric value. Source grade is not claim confidence.
methodology.corroboration: The six views reuse the existing archive. Similar stories, repeated posts, syndicated copy or multiple outlets quoting one origin are not independent corroboration. A human must inspect provenance.
methodology.geolocation: Location is shown only when supplied by the source or upstream archive. No location is inferred from a headline.
methodology.limits: This is open-source situational awareness, not intelligence agency coverage, an emergency warning service, a live market terminal or a verified threat assessment.
